page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by AWS Graviton2 processors running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a clock rate of 2.5 GHz. Each core has access to 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache, supported by a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without GPU accelerators, and features no local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage such as EBS for persistent data.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate moderate capabilities across raw compute and memory throughput metrics. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves an average single-core score of 1519.39 and a multi-core score of 6055.47. PassMark CPU testing yields a score of 2702.34, with extended instructions measuring 2482.25 and database operations reaching 2626.26. Geekbench testing reports 961.0 in single-core and 3217.0 in multi-core metrics, with clang compilation benchmarked at 4606.0. Memory bandwidth handles 72.78 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 35.07 GB/sec for write streams. Specialized workloads such as LLM inference underperform, generating 32.14 tokens/sec on small 135M models.

The hardware configuration trades complex vector extensions and attached local disks for balanced energy efficiency and consistent network baseline capacity. The architecture contains hardware AES support but lacks AVX, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets, restricting compute profiles that require complex x86 vector extensions. It is well matched for ARM-native scale-out microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web proxies, and light database workloads that fit within an 8.0 GB RAM footprint and leverage EBS storage over 6 Gbps network bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized ARM-based instance driven by 4 dedicated AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 cores at 2.5 GHz and 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, no GPUs, and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates stable throughput with stress-ng single-core performance at 1519.39 and multi-core at 6055.47, alongside Geekbench scores of 961.0 single-core and 3217.0 multi-core. The absence of x86 vector extensions like AVX-512 limits heavily vectorized calculations, while LLM inference speeds remain limited. With hardware-level AES support and balanced memory bandwidth, c6gn.xlarge is positioned for ARM-targeted CI/CD builds, network services, web servers, and distributed microservices reliant on EBS storage.
